issues.body: The new research record still hard-codes benchmark-style measurements throughout sections 6, 7, and 10: opcode totals, percentages, package-level deltas, synthetic-chain results, corpus sizes, and test-run counts. The companion program record repeats the same measurements in a table. Repository policy prohibits hard-coded performance numbers in Markdown and treats work-box measurements as non-canonical; describing the figures as non-canonical does not make embedding them compliant. This is materially the same major finding as round 2.
issues.fix_hint: Move raw opcode counts, percentages, package deltas, fixture results, and other quantitative run measurements into the repository's approved generated/result artifact mechanism. Link that artifact from both research Markdown files and retain only qualitative, evidence-bounded conclusions in the prose.
issues.title: Hard-coded performance measurements remain in Markdown

verdict.summary: Round 3 is stagnant. The same major policy violation from round 2 remains: both changed Markdown files embed extensive hard-coded performance measurements, including corpus opcode totals and percentages, per-package and synthetic-fixture deltas, test-run counts, and other quantitative results. Removing raw wall-clock seconds and labeling the remaining measurements non-canonical does not satisfy the repository's explicit prohibition on hard-coded performance numbers in Markdown. Move the quantitative measurements into the approved generated/result artifact mechanism and keep these research records qualitative and evidence-scoped, linking to that artifact.
